root_cause.text: The arm64 GCS mmap code used fixed _PAGE_GCS/_PAGE_GCS_RO PTE definitions that unconditionally included PTE_SHARED, even though under FEAT_LPA2 PTE bits 8-9 are repurposed as output address bits rather than shareability bits, causing invalid GCS page-table entries.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “bits 8-9 of the PTE replace the shareability attribute with bits 50-51 of the output address” when LPA2 is enabled, and the patch fixes this by introducing `gcs_page_prot` and explicitly clearing `PTE_SHARED` for GCS mappings in `adjust_protection_map()` (`gcs_page_prot &= ~PTE_SHARED;`) instead of directly using `_PAGE_GCS_RO`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused or redundant PAGE_GCS and PAGE_GCS_RO pgprot aliases while keeping the underlying GCS page protection encodings unchanged.
intent_record.what: Two preprocessor macro definitions, PAGE_GCS and PAGE_GCS_RO, which wrapped _PAGE_GCS and _PAGE_GCS_RO with __pgprot(...), were removed, while the underlying _PAGE_GCS and _PAGE_GCS_RO definitions were left unchanged.
intent_record.how: This eliminates the exported pgprot-style aliases for the GCS page attribute values, so code can no longer use PAGE_GCS or PAGE_GCS_RO from this header and must rely on the remaining lower-level definitions or other interfaces; in the shown hunk it does not alter the underlying page protection bit patterns themselves.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a read-only-after-init GCS page protection descriptor constant for future use in page mapping logic.
intent_record.what: A new file-scope static variable named gcs_page_prot of type ptdesc_t was added and marked __ro_after_init, initialized to _PAGE_GCS_RO immediately after the protection_map array definition.
intent_record.how: This introduces a read-only-after-init page table descriptor value representing GCS read-only page protection, making that protection setting available for later runtime use without changing behavior in this hunk by itself.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear `PTE_SHARED` from `gcs_page_prot` as well as `protection_map` when LPA2 is enabled to keep page protections consistent.
intent_record.what: The change wraps the existing `if (lpa2_is_enabled())` body in braces and adds a new statement inside it: `gcs_page_prot &= ~PTE_SHARED;`, alongside the existing loop that clears `PTE_SHARED` from every entry in `protection_map`.
intent_record.how: When LPA2 is enabled, the code now also clears the `PTE_SHARED` bit from `gcs_page_prot` at initialization time, ensuring this page protection setting is made consistent with the updated `protection_map` entries and preventing it from retaining an incompatible shared attribute.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the configured GCS page protection for shadow stack mappings instead of a hardcoded read-only GCS protection constant.
intent_record.what: The assignment in the VM_SHADOW_STACK and system_supports_gcs() branch of vm_get_page_prot() was changed from the hardcoded constant _PAGE_GCS_RO to the variable gcs_page_prot.
intent_record.how: At runtime, shadow stack mappings on systems that support GCS now use the page protection value stored in gcs_page_prot instead of always forcing _PAGE_GCS_RO, allowing the protection to reflect a configured or architecture-specific value rather than a fixed constant.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure shadow stack/GCS mappings consistently use the configured GCS page protection settings, including LPA2-related adjustments, rather than divergent hardcoded or incomplete protection handling.

relevance_review.reason: The change only removes unused/redundant PAGE_GCS and PAGE_GCS_RO aliases and explicitly keeps the underlying GCS PTE encodings unchanged. The root cause is the incorrect fixed _PAGE_GCS/_PAGE_GCS_RO encodings including PTE_SHARED under FEAT_LPA2, which this group does not address.
It changes the GCS page protection definitions used for page mappings, which is directly tied to the root cause involving incorrect fixed GCS PTE/protection definitions.

The root cause is incorrect hardcoded GCS PTE protections that still include PTE_SHARED under LPA2. This group directly fixes that by removing PTE_SHARED from gcs-specific protections when LPA2 is enabled and by making shadow stack/GCS mappings use the configured GCS page protection instead of hardcoded constants.

candidates.rationale: This hardcoded GCS protection bypasses the adjusted protection settings and directly uses the fixed _PAGE_GCS_RO definition, which according to the root cause unconditionally included PTE_SHARED and thus produced invalid PTEs under FEAT_LPA2.

This line shows that normal mmap protections had PTE_SHARED cleared when LPA2 is enabled, highlighting that GCS mappings were not receiving the same adjustment. The inconsistency is part of the root cause because the fixed GCS protection retained PTE_SHARED.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement hardcodes the GCS shadow stack mapping protection to _PAGE_GCS_RO. Per the root cause, the fixed _PAGE_GCS_RO PTE definition unconditionally included PTE_SHARED, which becomes invalid under FEAT_LPA2 because bits 8-9 are used for output address bits instead of shareability. Using this constant bypassed the adjusted protection settings intended to clear PTE_SHARED.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact GCS-specific mmap protection selection logic in `vm_get_page_prot()`. The vulnerable construct is present in the new GCS short-circuit: `if (system_supports_gcs() && (vm_flags & VM_SHADOW_STACK)) { prot = _PAGE_GCS_RO; }`. Per the stated root cause, `_PAGE_GCS/_PAGE_GCS_RO` were fixed PTE definitions that unconditionally included `PTE_SHARED`, which is invalid under FEAT_LPA2 because bits 8-9 become output address bits instead of shareability bits. This function directly assigns `_PAGE_GCS_RO` for shadow stack mappings and contains no conditional handling for LPA2 or alternate encoding of shareability. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet present.
